surfaces.part: muddy ground patch with ruts and puddle seen from above

answer.evidence: The whole 64x48 sprite is a flat ground decal seen from above: mud and grey-brown texture fills every row at full width (silhouette 64 across rows 0-47). The oily puddles (dark blue with teal edge and a few rainbow pixels near rows 20-28 and 36-44) lie flat in the texture. No front face, eave, edge line or vertical surface is drawn. This matches a flat floor decal, which has no front face by design.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts favour the candidate on tone count: 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outlines read as a dark brown mud tone rather than a sticker line. The weaknesses are structural. Near-flat coverage is 24% while both references are at 0%, and the board shows broad areas of one brown mud tone with only sparse speckle and a few crack lines. The whole patch uses only 19 distinct colours, and the mud ramp has about 4 steps against the references' 5-6. The two puddles are tiny, with only a couple of blue tones and little reflection or sheen. The rut hollows are barely visible, so the piece looks thinner and flatter than the reference tiles. Because of the flat-fill share and the shallow ramps, it would not sit comfortably next to the reference.
